learning_outcomes.text: Acquire knowledge related to the theory of cutting, tools, machine tools, and specific applications. The ultimate goal of accumulating this knowledge is to evaluate the limits and characteristics of various processing procedures, in order to make an appropriate selection based on the geometric configuration of parts, required precision, or material used.
Know the methods for establishing production types.
Define the specific principles of organizing production processes in time and space.
Master methods for preparing, programming, launching, and monitoring production.

syllabus_topics: Cutting tools (composition, constructive and functional angles, materials, tool wear and durability, deposits on the cutting edge)
Chip formation and geometry, mechanical stresses and thermal phenomena in the cutting process and cooling-lubricating fluids.
Bases of surface generation on machine tools
Production systems, specific processing procedures and equipment

assessment_methods.method: Evaluation of activity throughout the semester (including active participation in laboratory work, tests, and monitoring interest)

assessment_rules: A minimum final score of 50% is required for promotion, calculated by summing the weighted scores from the written exam (65%) and the semester activity evaluation (35%). Resit arrangements are not specified.
